decisions.reason: The guided historic mill tour reflects a visible heritage-and-hospitality commitment and any weak recent presence can plausibly be blamed on temporary pandemic-related disruptions, so management would tend to persist.

The sweet pastry fits the core business but appears to have lost visibility for an extended period and carries less distinctive public commitment, making it the easiest product for management to let go by now.

The crusty farmhouse bread is close to the established assortment, uses existing craft capabilities, and shows no clear negative signal strong enough to overcome management's tendency to continue recent launches.
The poppy seed Christmas stollen was presented as a flagship and backed by a gold award, so sunk promotional effort, public commitment, and strategic symbolism all strongly favor continuation.
The premium Christmas stollen also has an award and sits close to the firm's proven seasonal specialty range, so management would be reluctant to withdraw it absent clear failure evidence.
